source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting company losses in a financial disclosure

1. Start with the accounting records.
2.
completion:
Before taking any losses, calculate the valuation of the company based on its tax book value.
3. If losses are taken, keep a separate estimate of the company’s value as if no losses were taken.
4. Return to the accounting records and determine the amount of the loss.
5. Allocate all accumulated losses against the company’s assets, starting with the newest and least depreciated assets first. Continue until the losses are exhausted.
6. Consider the value of the company after the losses have been fully allocated against the assets. If it is zero, pause. If it is greater than zero, mark each asset to zero, starting with the oldest assets first and moving to the newest assets. As the assets are written off, allocate the total losses against the individual assets. Continue until the losses are exhausted or all assets are written off.

This process ensures that losses are accurately documented and reflected in the company’s financial statements.
